Answer: C
Reason: Comparing the 2003 and 2007 chest X-rays, there is a noticeable progression of fibrotic changes and increased pleural thickening/apical capping in the upper lobes. In patients with chronic fibrotic sarcoidosis, this structural distortion creates cavities that are prone to colonization by Aspergillus species, leading to the development of an aspergillus mycetoma (fungus ball), which is a well-known complication fitting this radiographic progression.
